contract: Bilingual, static multipage school website for families and school staff. The first screen identifies École Chrétienne Daniel in Fifadji, Cotonou; visitors can navigate the school, cycles, news, gallery and contact pages. No enrollment form, parent portal, unapproved media or unverified contact details. Target viewports: 390x844 and 1440x900.

accessibility.evidence: Browser checks confirmed keyboard-operable mobile navigation and disclosure, Escape closes and restores focus, language updates the document language/title/description and persists between routes, and reduced-motion mode leaves the motto illustration drawn. Representative text color pairs measured 4.95:1 to 13.78:1; interactive links and controls use visible focus styles and at least 44px heights where applicable.

responsive.evidence: All nine routes were measured at 390x844 and 1440x900. Each had document scrollWidth no greater than innerWidth; mobile measured 380/390px and desktop 1430/1440px. The gallery was visually reviewed at both target widths.

loading.reason: The pages and illustrations are local static assets; no asynchronous content loading is used.

empty.reason: The site has no dynamic listing or user-generated collection that can enter an empty state.

error.reason: There are no in-page submissions or remote data requests; external Facebook links leave the site.

partial.evidence: Unconfirmed phone, hours and admissions terms are explicitly marked as unverified. Facebook reporting is attributed to the visible posts and its media is not reproduced.

success.reason: No create, submit or save workflow is offered on these informational pages.

permission.reason: The gallery contains original illustrations only; adding school photos is deferred until the necessary permissions are confirmed.

renderedEvidence.observation: The desktop homepage presents the school identity, primary navigation, hero message and original book illustration without overlap.
The mobile gallery heading and introduction wrap cleanly; the responsive layout has no horizontal overflow.
The desktop gallery uses a clear editorial hierarchy and a three-column illustration layout.
